items.title: Live Updates: Germany’s Far Right Tops Key State Race, but Falls Short of Power
items.summary: The Alternative for Germany party is projected to finish first in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt. But lacking a majority, without the help of other parties it cannot become the first far-right party to govern a state since 1945.

items.title: U.S. Envoys Witkoff and Kushner Arrive in Kyiv After Talks With Putin
items.summary: Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met on Sunday with Volodymyr Zelensky in Kyiv, a day after talks with Vladimir V. Putin in Moscow.

items.title: Haitians Deported From U.S. Are Left Broke and Stranded
items.summary: Hundreds have been deported to Haiti in recent weeks, and some say they have been left with no money, no protection from gangs and no place to go.

items.title: In Germany, Ulrich Siegmund Is Bringing the AfD to the Cusp of Power
items.summary: Ulrich Siegmund, 35, once sold air fresheners. Now his far-right party is the favorite to win a state election in eastern Germany on Sunday.

items.title: In Ukraine, Fraud and Waste Are Rewarded With More Weapons Contracts
items.summary: Secret military audits reveal a military procurement system riddled with mismanagement. In 2024 alone, Ukraine lost $1.2 billion to fraud and waste.

items.title: A Bad Year for Bees Gets Worse as Trump’s Tariffs Hit Canada’s Honey Belt
items.summary: Alberta produces 40 percent of Canada’s honey. This year, rain and President Trump’s trade war have combined to threaten the industry.

items.title: China’s New Graduates, Facing a Dire Job Market, Must Also Contend With A.I.
items.summary: A record 12.7 million young people are looking for jobs as the country embraces artificial intelligence — and as the technology begins to upend the work force.

items.title: Here Is Where Ukraine Peace Talks Stand, as a New Round Approaches
items.summary: A deadly campaign of Russian and Ukrainian airstrikes has escalated since the last U.S.-brokered negotiations stalled in February.

items.title: Germany’s AfD Could Win Its First State Government. Here’s What to Know.
items.summary: The Alternative for Germany dominated the vote in Saxony-Anhalt, though it appeared to fall short of an absolute majority.

items.title: Putin Meets Witkoff and Kushner in Moscow to Discuss Ukraine War
items.summary: President Vladimir V. Putin ordered a pause in strikes on Ukraine’s capital, Kyiv, ahead of the meeting with President Trump’s envoys: his son-in-law Jared Kushner and the businessman Steve Witkoff.

items.title: Oil Prices Rise Slightly After U.S. and Iran Trade Strikes
items.summary: Brent crude, the global benchmark for oil, was up about 1 percent as trading resumed on Sunday, while the national average price of gas was nearly $4.15 a gallon.

items.title: Cargo Plane Crashes at Miami Airport, Striking Vehicles
items.summary: Officials said 5 others were injured. Flights were halted for hours at Miami International Airport after the Boeing 767-300 cargo plane overran its landing.

items.title: OPEC Plus Holds Oil Production Steady as U.S.-Iran Strikes Resume
items.summary: The decision on Sunday by the cartel of oil-producing nations and some of its allies came after the resumption of U.S. and Iranian military strikes in the Persian Gulf.

items.title: Iran’s Attacks Keep the Strait of Hormuz in a Lethal Stalemate
items.summary: The U.S. military is helping oil get out of the Persian Gulf on tankers, but Iran is still attacking the ships and scaring operators away.

items.title: How a Blacklisted Chinese Tech Giant Kept Buying America’s Best A.I. Chips
items.summary: Washington imposed sanctions on Inspur because of its work with the Chinese military. But the company’s subsidiary kept shipping Nvidia’s best chips to feed China’s leading A.I. firms.

items.title: The C.E.O. Teaching Future Generations About 9/11
items.summary: Elizabeth Hillman, chief of the 9/11 Memorial & Museum since 2022, says the stories of that day “remain compelling, and they’re still unfolding.”

items.title: CCRCs Are Expanding Retirement Home Care to Seniors’ Own Homes
items.summary: Continuing care retirement communities are widening their scope to help retirees age in place, with measured supports and a way to cap the soaring costs of aging.

items.title: How Victoria’s Secret Is Reviving Its Pink Brand
items.summary: After Pink’s sales slipped in recent years, Victoria Secret’s new chief executive is focused on making women feel bold and flirty.

items.title: ‘Go Get Your Kicks’: The Europeans Obsessed With a U.S. Highway
items.summary: As Route 66 turns 100, tourists in search of Americana try to keep war, inflation and politics in the rearview.

items.title: E. Coli Illnesses Linked to Frozen Blueberries Are Up to 17, F.D.A. Says
items.summary: The affected frozen fruit products, which were distributed to 19 states and to retailers like Walmart and Publix, were recalled starting in July.

items.title: Kenyans Made a Living Writing College Essays. Then A.I. Arrived.
items.summary: Thousands of Kenyans made a living writing essays for overseas students. With A.I., the work has dried up, a warning for online gig work that has been a global lifeline.

items.title: Court Filings In A.I. Suit Invoke Copyright Law, Culture and Sports
items.summary: Filings made Friday in The New York Times’s closely watched lawsuit against OpenAI and Microsoft included a range of copyright law and cultural references.

items.title: Why the Hugging Face Hack Should Make You Worry More About A.I.
items.summary: The attack by an aggressive “collective” of OpenAI agents shows the danger of artificial intelligence systems that organize themselves.

items.title: Authors Wrangle With Publishers Over $1.5 Billion Anthropic A.I. Settlement
items.summary: The tech giant must pay $3,000 per pirated book that it used to train its chatbot. Many authors fear they could lose funds to others in the book business.

items.title: The Generation That’s Never Had to Say ‘Hello?’
items.summary: Now that there’s rarely any mystery to who’s calling, Gen Z has adopted a range of custom phone greetings — including no greeting at all.

items.title: F.B.I. Investigates Sale of Millions of Stolen Driver’s Licenses
items.summary: The blog Krebs on Security reported on an identity theft service trying to sell scans of licenses and other documents belonging to people in Canada and the United States.

items.title: Tumbler Ridge Shooting Survivors File 30 Lawsuits Against OpenAI
items.summary: The survivors contend that the company should have notified the police when it shut down the shooter’s disturbing ChatGPT account eight months before the February attack in British Columbia.

items.title: Corporate America Is Getting Hooked on Open-Source A.I.
items.summary: Companies like AT&T are increasingly using cheap, freely available artificial intelligence models over expensive ones from Anthropic and OpenAI.

items.title: Tesla’s Cybercab Is Being Investigated by Federal Regulators
items.summary: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration said it would examine whether the company’s new self-driving taxi, which has no steering wheel, meets federal auto regulations.
